entries.title: Call of Cthulhu: Shadow of the Comet

emulation.notes: Use the store-provided DOSBox configuration rather than manually sourcing old disks.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Authentic DOS-era presentation with modern PC compatibility.

primary.why: The modern Windows PC digital release is the best route because it legally packages the DOS adventure for current machines, with the Steam page noting both CD-ROM and floppy versions and GOG documenting a DOSBox-powered release.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Call of Cthulhu: Shadow of the Comet on Steam or GOG and run the bundled DOSBox version on Windows PC; use the CD-ROM version where the launcher offers it.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a compatibility-packaged classic release, not a visual remaster.

entries.title: Call of Cthulhu: Prisoner of Ice

emulation.notes: Use the current Steam/GOG package for easiest setup.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Authentic classic adventure presentation with modern PC compatibility.

primary.why: The modern Windows PC digital release is the best route because it makes the original computer adventure readily playable on current PCs, while the Japanese Saturn and PlayStation ports are sourced as having no enhancements over the PC versions.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Call of Cthulhu: Prisoner of Ice on Steam or GOG and run the bundled PC/DOSBox release on Windows.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a compatibility-packaged classic release, not a visual remaster.

entries.title: Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth

emulation.notes: Use the GOG release when possible; consult community fix notes if using Steam.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC resolution/capture route with compatibility fixes.

primary.why: The Windows PC route is the strongest route because it has native PC resolution/capture flexibility, and the GOG release includes several small fixes pre-applied. The Xbox release is historically first but has no exclusive content advantage.
primary.how_to_play: Buy the GOG Windows release for the pre-applied fixes. If using Steam instead, check first for known bug and unofficial-fix notes before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster; the PC version is known for bugs, so prefer the GOG release or vetted community fixes.

entries.title: Call of Cthulhu: The Wasted Land
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release if already owned

emulation.notes: Use an owned Windows PC copy if available; otherwise wait for a legal re-release.

primary.version: PC release / Steam build if already owned
primary.why: The Windows PC route is the best available play target because it gives the tactical RPG a larger-screen capture route than the mobile releases. Availability is the caveat: public delisting trackers report the Steam/App Store/Google Play versions were delisted, so this is mainly for owners or any future legal re-release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC/Steam build if it is already in your library. If not, wait for a legal re-release rather than using an unsourced mobile APK.

entries.remaster_caveats: The game appears delisted from major storefronts; do not rely on unofficial APK mirrors as a definitive play route.

entries.title: Call of Cthulhu

emulation.notes: Use the native PC release for capture and settings control.

primary.why: The Windows PC release is the best main route because it is the same full Cyanide/Focus game with PC capture/settings flexibility, while the PS4, Xbox One, and Switch releases have no sourced exclusive story or gameplay content.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Call of Cthulhu on Steam and play the Windows PC build; look into any display or compatibility tweaks before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: No separate remaster or definitive edition is documented for the 2018 game.
